definitions.explanation: sending liquid, gas, or other material through pipes or channels using applied pressure

examples.japanese: コンクリートをポンプで{圧送|あっそう}する。
{圧送|あっそう}{管|かん}を{通|つう}じて{汚水|おすい}を{処理場|しょりじょう}に{送|おく}る。
examples.english: Wastewater is sent to the treatment plant through a pressure pipe.

examples.japanese: {高層|こうそう}ビルの{上階|じょうかい}に{水|みず}を{届|とど}けるためには、{強力|きょうりょく}なポンプで{圧送|あっそう}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: To deliver water to the upper floors of a high-rise building, powerful pumps are needed to force it through under pressure.

notes:
A technical term used in construction, plumbing, and engineering for moving materials through pipes using applied pressure. Most commonly encountered in concrete pumping ({生|なま}コン{圧送|あっそう}) at construction sites and in wastewater management.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {圧送|あっそう}ポンプ: pressure pump
- {圧送|あっそう}{管|かん}: pressure pipe
- コンクリート{圧送|あっそう}: concrete pumping
- {圧送|あっそう}{方式|ほうしき}: pressure-feed system

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {送水|そうすい}: water delivery — sending water, not necessarily under pressure
- {加圧|かあつ}: pressurization — applying pressure in general, not specifically for sending material
- {揚水|ようすい}: water pumping/lifting — pumping water upward, as from a well
